value.rationale: The isolated sixth Fourier zero is the earliest nonconsecutive additional null after the first two that excludes the regular-three-node sharp gap construction: added frequencies four and five vanish on that construction. This makes the exact support-gap threshold a natural new sparse-quadrature invariant. The result improves the sharp 2π/3 two-moment bound to an explicit strict algebraic constant and classifies all equality measures; these are not a routine rephrasing of the consecutive-band theorem.
